relevance: Timing of guidance injection is a harness design lever.

media.description: Abstract excerpt auditing what event a coding-agent harness's 'guidance before first edit' gate actually intercepts, using local Qwen2.5-Coder 14B agents and file hashing in a 76-arm study.
media.ocr_text: When a coding-agent harness promises guidance before the first source edit, what event does it actually intercept? We audit five separate events: policy assignment, request eligibility, trigger, plan delivery, and observed source-content change. A prescribed-action comparison exposes the coverage of three gate rules but cannot tell us how an agent would continue after receiving a plan. We therefore run local agents on public software issues and hash Python files before and after each executed action. In a pilot-guided, 76-arm study using Qwen2.5-Coder 14B, 15 arms change Python source across seven tasks and three repositories. Guidance precedes every observed first change, but every change uses a structured editor and the study misses its prespecified 20-arm coverage target.
